# Results — Study 772 (Album-Drop)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**Spotify (SPOT) moves on a blockbuster album release**: rallies into the drop, pops (or
fades) after. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month).
Fingerprint `5406b18c6109` (SPOT + SPY, one combined panel, adjusted/total-return daily
closes).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, `SPOT` (Spotify) + `SPY` (S&P 500), one combined panel: 2,072 rows, 2018-04-03 → 2026-06-30 |
| Calendar | **hardcoded**: 27 blockbuster album drops 2018-06→2024-11 (Drake, Taylor Swift, Adele, Bad Bunny, Beyoncé, Billie Eilish…), real release dates from artist/label press releases — all after Spotify's 2018-04-03 direct listing |
| Events resolvable | all **27** of 27 drops have SPOT+SPY coverage around the anchor |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of the abnormal return (SPOT − SPY) across independent, non-overlapping album events (the correct unit — not a daily panel); Wilson hit-rate interval; a 20-seed × 200-draw random-window placebo per cut; leave-one-out jackknife |
| Execution / costs | **calendar-known, zero look-ahead**: album dates are announced weeks ahead (pre-orders, teaser singles). Run-up = [anchor−K → anchor]; reaction = [anchor → anchor+K]; net of 2× one-way cost × NAV. Gross AND net reported |
| Price basis | **total-return** (dividends reinvested, `auto_adjust=True`) for both legs |

**Beta, named:** SPOT is a high-beta growth name, so a raw `SPOT − SPY` difference over any
drifting window is partly mechanical. The run-up/reaction windows here are short (2–4
weeks), so beta is a minor contaminant — but it is the reason we quote the *abnormal*
return throughout, never the raw SPOT move.

## The run-up — abnormal return, K sessions BEFORE the drop (SPOT − SPY)

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week run-up (k=10) | 27 | +0.219% | +0.123 | 10/27 = 37.0% [21.5%, 55.8%] |
| 1-month run-up (k=21) | 27 | +1.436% | +0.602 | 15/27 = 55.6% [37.3%, 72.4%] |

The "buy SPOT into the drop" half is a **clean zero**: in the two weeks (or month) into a
blockbuster release, SPOT is statistically indistinguishable from SPY (both cuts
|*t*| < 0.65). There is no rally to front-run.

## The reaction — abnormal return, K sessions AFTER the drop

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week reaction (k=10) | 27 | −1.158% | −0.709 | 14/27 = 51.9% [34.0%, 69.3%] |
| 1-month reaction (k=21) | 27 | −1.622% | −0.928 | 13/27 = 48.1% [30.7%, 66.0%] |

The post-drop reaction is *slightly* negative on average but nowhere near significant
(both |*t*| < 1, hit rate ≈ coin-flip). A record-breaking streaming week simply does not
move the stock: Spotify's revenue is subscription (ARPU × MAU), not a per-stream cut that
one mega-album meaningfully shifts.

## Random-window placebo (20 seeds × 200 draws per event)

| cut | tail | observed | placebo mean (sd) | p |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week run-up | right | +0.219% | +0.368% (1.557%) | 0.533 |
| 2-week reaction | right | −1.158% | +0.368% (1.557%) | 0.833 |

Both cuts sit inside the luck cloud (p ≈ 0.53 and 0.83) — the observed means are ordinary
tracking noise, exactly what a random 2-week SPOT-vs-SPY window looks like.

## Jackknife (leave-one-out) — 2-week reaction *t*

Full-sample *t* = **−0.709**; across all 27 leave-one-out draws the *t* stays in
**[−1.178, −0.275]** — never approaching significance, so there is no single hero (or
villain) album driving even the tiny negative tilt.

## Tradability — net of costs (calendar-known entry, zero look-ahead)

| window | gross | net @ 5 bps | net @ 10 bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2-week run-up | +0.219% (*t* +0.12) | +0.119% (*t* +0.07) | +0.019% (*t* +0.01) |
| 2-week reaction | −1.158% (*t* −0.71) | −1.258% (*t* −0.77) | −1.358% (*t* −0.83) |

Nothing to bank. The run-up is a rounding error before costs and zero after them; the
reaction is a noisy negative that never clears significance. There is no edge in any cut,
gross or net.

## Synthetic positive control (deterministic, no network)

- **Null (bump = 0), 20 seeds:** mean *t* = +0.11 (sd 1.21); |*t*| ≥ 2 in **2/20** seeds —
  a well-behaved small-sample false-positive rate at n = 27 events with a 10-day AR.
- **Planted run-up +1.0% (seed 776):** mean AR +2.02%, *t* = **+2.16**.
- **Planted run-up +2.0% (seed 776):** mean AR +3.02%, *t* = **+3.23** — a real bump is
  recovered monotonically, so the detector would have found a genuine album effect had one
  existed.

## Verdict

| Axis | Stamp | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Signal — is the effect real?** | **None** | Every real cut is indistinguishable from noise: run-up +0.22% (*t* +0.12) and +1.44% (*t* +0.60); reaction −1.16% (*t* −0.71) and −1.62% (*t* −0.93). All |*t*| < 1, hit rates ≈ coin-flip, placebo p = 0.53 / 0.83 (dead-centre), jackknife never near significance — while the synthetic control cleanly recovers a planted +1%/+2% bump. The effect isn't weak, it's absent. |
| **Tradability — survives costs/scale?** | **Mirage** | Nothing to bank. The run-up is a rounding error that vanishes after costs; the reaction is a sub-1-*t* negative. No edge in any window, gross or net. |

**In one sentence:** a chart-smashing album drop lights up the streaming charts but leaves
Spotify's *stock* untouched — the "buy SPOT into the drop" trade is folklore, because one
record week is a rounding error against a subscription business the market has already
priced.
